# Summary of the Labour Party Manifesto 2019

The Labour Party's 2019 manifesto, titled "It's Time for Real Change," presents a comprehensive vision for transforming Britain across multiple policy areas, with a focus on addressing inequality, climate change, and public services.

## Core Economic Vision

Labour proposes rewriting economic rules to benefit ordinary people rather than privileged elites. They plan a £400 billion National Transformation Fund to upgrade the economy, including £250 billion specifically for green transformation. A National Investment Bank backed by Regional Development Banks would provide £250 billion in lending over ten years. The party promises to bring rail, mail, water, and energy into public ownership and deliver free full-fibre broadband to all homes.

## Green Industrial Revolution

Central to the manifesto is tackling the climate emergency through creating one million green jobs, achieving net-zero carbon energy within the 2030s, upgrading 27 million homes for energy efficiency, and investing in renewable energy. Labour pledges to ban fracking permanently and support workers transitioning from fossil fuel industries.

## Public Services

The NHS would receive average 4.3% annual spending increases, with Labour promising to end privatisation, provide free prescriptions and dental check-ups, and protect the service from trade negotiations. They propose a National Care Service offering free personal care for older people. The National Education Service would provide free education throughout life, including abolished tuition fees, restored maintenance grants, and expanded early years provision.

## Workers' Rights

Labour promises the "biggest extension of workers' rights in history," including a £10 minimum wage for all ages, ending zero-hours contracts, establishing a Ministry for Employment Rights, strengthening trade union powers, and reducing average working hours to 32 per week within a decade.

## Social Security and Housing

The manifesto pledges to scrap Universal Credit and design a dignity-based alternative, lift children and pensioners from poverty, and maintain pension triple-lock. On housing, Labour proposes building over one million council and social homes, ending right-to-buy, introducing rent controls, and ending rough sleeping within five years.

## Brexit Position

Labour offers a final say referendum within six months, with choices between a renegotiated deal (including a customs union and Single Market alignment) and remaining in the EU.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposals include abolishing the House of Lords, reducing voting age to 16, and establishing a Constitutional Convention to redistribute power throughout the UK.
